title.narrative: Abu Salama Society in Red Sea - Ababda tribe’s women sustainable employment through recycling handicrafts in Wadi El Gimal National Park
Abu Salama Society in Red Sea - Ababda tribe’s women sustainable employment through recycling handicrafts in Wadi El Gimal National Park

description.narrative:
Wadi el Gimal national park (WGNP) in Red Sea Governorate, 50 km south of Marsa Alam town. WGNP encompasses a segment of important natural habitats along the coast. It is inhabited by local pastoral peoples belonging to the Ababda Tribe, still practice a traditional lifestyle in harmony with their environment, their main economic activities is gazing camel and fishing. Women of Ababda tribes preserve their heritage through produce handicrafts targeting the visitors in WGNP. The coral reef, mangroves forest, turtles and also local community suffer from the accelerated solid and plastics waste as results for tourist growth along the coast and also from the climate change impact.
The project will develop the skills and train 230 women in WGNP in produce handicrafts from recycling and up cycling the plastics, glass, camel bones leftover, goats leather, palm tree leftover and help for generate new jobs in the same time to raise awareness of women and visitors about climate change and nature conservation. The recycling materials will come from the local landfill and also the cleanup campaigns. The project’s duration will be 12 months.
